genZNote: The name literally means 'big beast' — one of the largest bacterial cells known, and it's completely harmless.

morphology.shape: Large rod (bacillus), among the largest known bacterial cells

habitat.naturalHabitat: Soil, decaying organic matter, and various environmental niches worldwide
habitat.hostAssociation: Not host-associated — a free-living environmental saprophyte
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Extremely widespread in soil; endospores allow long-term environmental survival

microscopy.stain: Gram stain, malachite green spore stain
microscopy.appearance: Large Gram-positive rods with central to subterminal endospores

culture.growthCharacteristics: Obligate aerobe, grows readily at room temperature to 37°C

identificationClues: One of the largest known bacterial cells — visibly large rods on Gram stain
Ubiquitous soil saprophyte, essentially non-pathogenic to humans
Used industrially as a recombinant protein production host

diseases: Not a recognized human pathogen; occasional reports of contamination or pseudo-outbreak isolates in clinical specimens
clinicalImportance.transmission: Not applicable — environmental exposure, not infectious transmission
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Of biotechnological rather than clinical importance; used as an expression host for recombinant protein production due to its high secretion capacity
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: May be recovered as an environmental contaminant in cultures and should be distinguished from pathogenic Bacillus species (B. anthracis, B. cereus) by clinical context and biochemical profile

examFacts.importantTest: Spore stain and colony/cell size help distinguish from other Bacillus species
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Among the largest bacterial cells known; widely used as an industrial protein-expression host
